channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: A New Era Of Police Surveillance Is Coming To Hawai‘i
item.description: Drones are already used by law enforcement for special operations, but the program coming to Waikīkī marks a major increase in police surveillance and will be the first time Hawaiʻi uses drones as first responders.

item.title: Are Media Mergers Good For Hawaiʻi?
item.description: Massive consolidation is washing up on our shores. Let's hope state regulators are paying attention.

item.title: Hawaiʻi Sen. Michelle Kidani Says She’s Capable Of Handling Her Job
item.description: The 77-year-old lawmaker is trying to defuse concerns that she suffers from an illness that is affecting her performance.

item.title: Higher Luxury Home Taxes? State Eyes New Ways To House Hawaiians
item.description: The Department of Hawaiian Home Lands will need billions in additional revenue to provide homes for the roughly 30,000 Hawaiians on its waitlist.

item.title: What The Immigration Debate Misses About Place And Belonging
item.description: Human beings should be treated humanely. It's a basic moral minimum, not a political vision.

item.title: Governor Asks Lawmakers For $126M In Green Fee Projects
item.description: Some lawmakers are questioning the administration's plan to fund the projects through a combination of the new fee and bonds.

item.title: Will Disaster Insurance Overhaul Increase Protections For Future Survivors?
item.description: Other states impacted by similar disasters are reforming their insurance laws. Legislators here are teeing up bills to follow suit.

item.title: Word Row: Feb. 5
item.description: Our six-letter version of this popular game.

item.title: He Mau Pilikia Mea Kaʻahele Ma Dillingham Ma Muli O Ke Kūkulu Alakau
item.description: Ua wāwahi nā limahana kūkulu i nā alanui a me nā alahele, a he ʻaʻe ʻia paha o kekahi mau kānāwai ADA.

item.title: Red Hill Victims Dealt A Blow In Their Fight Against The Navy
item.description: Plaintiffs said they didn't know about fuel samples until it was too late. The judge declined their request to punish the government.
